Set a Shiny input from an endpoint

Source: R/session.R
spigot_trigger.Rd

spigot_trigger() sets input[[name]] in a tab's Shiny session to value, so the app's reactive code (observeEvent(input$cart, ...), reactive(), outputs) runs as if the page had changed an input. Use it when an API call should update a live view that the server function builds. Most endpoints do not need it: return the data, or push it with spigot_emit().

Usage

spigot_trigger(session, name, value)

Arguments

session

The Shiny session from spigot_session(), or a server function's session.

name

Input name: a letter, then letters, digits, _, . or -.

value

Any R value.

Value

TRUE, invisibly.

Details

The input is set the normal Shiny way: spigot asks the page, and the page calls Shiny.setInputValue() with priority: "event". So the observers run in a regular reactive flush, and every trigger fires them, even with the same value as the last one. It takes one extra trip over the websocket, about as long as any input change takes Shiny.

value itself never leaves R: the page sends back only an id, and input[[name]] is identical() to value. Data frames, factors, dates, NA and objects JSON cannot hold arrive unchanged. The value is kept in the session until the page sends the id back (or the session ends).

Because the page sets the input, the trigger reaches the observers after the endpoint has returned, and only if the page is open and loaded spigot.js (every spigot page does). Called with a module's session, name is namespaced like the module's own inputs.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
#* @post /cart/add
function(req, sku) {
  s <- spigot::spigot_session(req)
  cart <- add_to_cart(s$userData$cart_id, sku)
  spigot::spigot_trigger(s, "cart", cart)
  list(ok = TRUE)
}

# In the server function:
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$total <- renderText(sum(input$cart$price))
}
} # }
